title: Pressure in Fluids

problems_fixed.what: Duplicate answer within tier: bronze[0] and bronze[5] both gave 3000 Pa (600/0.2 and 900/0.3). Changed the force 900 N -> 1200 N so p = 1200/0.3 = 4000 Pa, distinct and clean. Updated display, SVG label, solution, hint, misconception and walk.

figures_note: All 15 problems already carried an SVG figure. Added role="img" + aria-label to each (validator + a11y), stripped the redundant xmlns=http://... namespace (tripped the external-resources check on inline SVG), and neutralised em dashes/— inside SVG comments and captions. Zero new figures drawn; none were missing.

guided_conversion.opener_concept: Skis vs stiletto heel on snow: same 600 N weight, wildly different area, so wildly different squash. Box 1 (600 divided by 2) is pure common sense; the reveal names it as pressure p = F / A and links to p = hrho g.
guided_conversion.teach_walks: Bronze: substitute straight in (p = F/A). Silver: rearrange first (h = p/(rho g)). Gold: chain two equations (p = hrho g then F = pA).
guided_conversion.walk_ritual: Every bank walk: state equation (say), identify the value, compute (phase:substitute), then a reversal check that lands back on a given value; final done-note states the answer WITH its unit. No unit-conversion box needed: every given value is already in base units (m, kg/m3, m2, N, Pa).

misconceptions: Every misconception given a determinate expect derived by committing a real error (inverse_error: multiply/divide swap; forgot_step: dropping the x10 for g, or using full depth instead of depth difference, or stopping at pressure without the force). All expects verified outside the +/-0.011 accept window.
